english_verification.review_scope: Representative current-Mod opening identity, academy/apotheosis route and the actual fixed-revision English Wiki history chunk; corrected native names Karodir I Varamzuir and Alarel Aralzuir where applicable; no exhaustive mission or national-idea audit. Native English national-idea names and descriptions were compared by localisation key by the primary. Large source intervals are locator envelopes, not a claim to inspect every intervening line or establish complete runtime reachability.
unresolved: The Wiki records the academy's 1446 foundation, which is later than the 1444 opening and does not certify an already completed academy.
No standalone Wiki page was used to certify every current mechanic or every mission branch.
Alarel Aralzuir is retained as the current Mod consort name but is not asserted as a Wiki-derived historical claim.

rationale.campaign_length: The 24 dedicated definitions are followed by long-term research and formation preparation.
rationale.colonization: The main route read for this entry is not centred on overseas colonisation.
rationale.complexity: Buildings, research, resources and ruler status must be prepared in parallel.
rationale.dark_story: Severe experimental losses and tiered apotheosis provide a dark turn.
rationale.difficulty: Research thresholds and ruler risk increase difficulty; no live playtest was performed.
rationale.diplomacy: The main diplomatic work coordinates estates, religious orders and neighbours rather than building an alliance web.
rationale.early_pressure: A weak geopolitical position and stronger neighbours create early pressure.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The opening mage and the god-making project run through the whole campaign.
rationale.narrative_density: A small kingdom's revival, its academy and the divine experiment form a continuous story.
rationale.tall_play: The academy, university and mage tower are the central long-term investments.
rationale.trade_economy: Resources such as glass, porcelain and wine affect the research prerequisites.
rationale.warfare: War against stronger neighbours and expansion in Bulwar serve the research state's need for room.

identity.appearance: Sun Elf kingdom existing in 1444, ruled by the powerful mage Karodir I Varamzuir.
identity.formation_scope: Can conditionally form the Phoenix Empire (F38/F97); countries that were formerly F42 retain potential access to the Varamhar route.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
The House of Knowledge of the Magical Arts, commonly known as the University of Ulmiš Idiqlat, was founded in 1446 by Karodir I Varamzuir, and quickly became the primary center of learning and study of magic in Bulwar. The university gained massive popularity when the king revoked the ban on human magi in his kingdom after the death of Taelarios of Irrliam, tripling the amount of magi of the institution.

During the Jadd Empire, Ulmiš Idiqlat remained an important and prestigious site even after the founding of other universities such as those in Brasan, Medurubar, and Jaddanzar during the Magi Renaissance. It opened education to all; however, it offered the widest array of courses to those who focus on the Sun Elf scholarly magic, and the Bulwari magic of Order.

Under the Divine-herald Tezalindor the Kind, the university became the first secular institution enabled to teach the Bulwari magic of Light, something that Karodir aimed for when he established it, training a new generation of Exorcist-priests who relied on arcane magic rather than divine.

description.text:
After the Great Assembly of Bulwar, King Daryam of Gišhuram gave a plot of land to Varamar, a distinguished captain of the Phoenix Legions, who founded the city of Varamhar alongside his subordinates.

Since its foundation, and especially during the war against Harpylen and later after the fall of the Jexisian Empire, Varamhar has had to deal with harpy raids and incursions. So Varamar had a special unit trained, the White Phoenix Guard, who were made up of highly mobile troops that would be able to swiftly respond to the threats of harpies and could quickly be deployed for defense or aid.

description.text: One of the benefits of having a university tied to your government is the access to a large pool of fresh talent. And both Varamhar and the Jadd Empire eagerly made use of that. Karodir instituted, and the Jadd Empire maintained, an obligatory internship period in government offices for all who attended the Academy. Magi were prized. Many of them aided the government in its daily tasks, while the most talented were offered military posts or moved on to secret projects.

description.text: One of the great delicacies of Bulwar is Jaherian Sunlight. It is a sweet white wine made of raisins long-fermented in the sun. There are but a few locations throughout Bulwar where it is bottled, and its rarity has made it highly prized among the Cannorian upper class. However, the highest quality wine is made in Varamhar, and getting hold of a bottle of Varamhar Jaherian Sunlight is a clear sign of status.

description.text: After the fall of the Jexisian Empire, Bulwar divided itself among the local elven governors. Some thrived and drew powers to themselves while others shattered like the Kingdom of Dalarand during the Second Cinder War. Within this chaos, Kelindil Varamzuir, right hand of the king of Dalarand, plotted against his king with the Twelve of Bulwar to assassinate him. The plot was successful, and Kelindil carved his kingdom of Dalarand at the end of the war. His successors also learned to deal with the deck they were given, relying not on military might but on subterfuge to retain their independence as the weakest kingdom of the Suran Plain.

description.text:
Harpy raids had historically been a nightmare for merchants traveling through Bulwar, especially close to the Hills. In antiquity, the kingdom of Gišhuram responded with a program of construction: roofed cities to protect against harpy raids.

Many of those protections were in disrepair when Varamhar was established, but the rising menace of Ayarallen forced the Varamhari crown to restore the roof protections to their former glory. In exchange, they gained the love of the populace and a reputation of reliance among merchants, as they were much more eager to trade in a location where they or their goods did not just suddenly get carried away by an unexpected flock of harpies.

But Karodir not only repaired the existing Bazaar cities but improved them. Gišhuram, the city of astrologers and Varamhar’s capital, was protected with a roof composed of enchanted bronze tiles that could be retracted using magic. This allowed to increase the defensiveness of Varamhar’s capital while at the same time allowing the citizens to keep the view of the night sky from the city streets.

description.text:
Unlike other Sun Elves who prefer close-combat spells, the Erdmagi are Varamhari magi specialized in powerful long-distance spells, a combination of Sun Elven traditions and the Bulwari magic of Order. These spells are costly and difficult to apply on the battlefields of the Suran Plain, where cavalry is king, but they are especially effective against stationary targets, such as walls, and slow-moving targets like siege engines or disciplined enemy formations.

During the siege of Gišhuram by the Desert Legion, the Erdmagi managed to keep the enemy at bay despite the city being attacked by both sides of the Buranun. Resisting the siege for over a year, the city surrendered after the death of Araš of Akalšes, when Karodir was released from the dungeons of Arašbar and was allowed to go into exile in exchange for his kingdom.

While some of the Erdmagi followed Karodir and joined the Jaherian Exemplars, most of them remained and joined the ranks of the nascent Jadd Empire, being renowned for their participation in the wars in Rahen against the Command.

description.text:
"The conqueror stood at the world far edge and stared across the sunlit sea,
And felt aught but crushing darkness, No thrill of victory.
His blood sang for conquest but the world had struck him lame,
And he wept great tears of fire and in thundering voice proclaimed.
"I have reached my zenith, the highest I shall mark,
For there are no more worlds to conquer, my soul is torn apart."
He turned to face his empire, resigned to his fate,
Jaher's time had passed, his death he did await.
Till one takes up the mantle.
The Phoenix Crown awaits."
-from the Litany of Jaher by Sarada Razumir

description.text: The Sun Elves have long been styled the Chosen of Surael, destined to pave the way for his glorious return. Yet even as the Empire rose from the ashes of Jexis' reign there was a significant minority within its borders who refused to follow the true faith, not to mention those outside the Empire who still clung to dead gods. To combat this the priests of Surael formed The Order of the Light of Truth to spread the teachings of the Sun Temple to the farthest corners of the world, a task they proved apt in achieving.

description.text: The Phoenix Empire is one of soaring temples and palaces that reach towards the heavens, from the Palace of Eternal Fire to the Dawn temple its lands are filled with wonders undreamed, draped in marble and gold. It is not uncommon for the Elvish nobility to have sprawling estates larger than most towns as they add grander and grander edifices as the centuries wear on. With its resurgence the new Emperors undertook great projects to craft edifices to surpass anything found in the kingdoms of man and cement the glory of a new age of Elven leadership and peace.

description.text:
In years past Jaher and Jexis lead the finest armies that the world has ever seen in their conquests. Legends of endless ranks of Legionaries clad in glittering golden armour and armed with shining silver blades are told across all of Cannor. Since the fall of Jexis the proud warrior traditions of the Phoenix Legions has faded into history and no more golden warriors march across Sarhal for the glory of the Sun Elf people.

Now that our great Empire has been reformed from the ashes, so too must the Legions march. For too long have those blades of legend been left to rust and dull under the weight of years. Once more the Phoenix Legions shall rise and once more the enemies of the Sun Elves shall tremble at their passing.

description.text: Trade is one of the most vital practices in the Empire, much of the Elves' vast wealth is drawn from eastern goods traveling along the Empire's trade routes to be sold in the western lands of Cannor. To facilitate this trade, as well as to give an edge to their own merchant class, the Imperial government set about establishing a series of way stations called The Offices of Trade throughout its vast holdings where their merchants could rest and prepare for long journeys.

description.text: In the imperial capital of Bulwar, near to the Imperial Palace, lies a vast and sprawling complex of gold and lapis lazuli. Its official name is the Imperial Academy of Progress but most know it by another name The Gilded Menagerie. It is here that the future governors of the Empire are trained, many a noble house has sent its scions here in order to gain favour and position within the Imperial Bureaucracy. Its darker purpose is the training ground of the Empire's vast network of spies and assassins. It is said that in every court in Cannor, in every gathering of mages the Menagerie has a dozen sets of ears listening to every word and a dozen sharpened knives at every back.

description.text: The Phoenix Empire and its Sun Elf rulers are masters over vast and diverse lands stretching from horizon to horizon. It is within this Empire more than any other that cultures meet, trade and mingle under the enlightened rule of the chosen. The Sun Elves have accepted their destiny as those who will one day lead the entire world under their glorious rule and accept all the lesser races and accept all into the fold, provided they kneel at the feet of their betters.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid it if you dislike waiting for multiple prerequisites or accepting ruler and experimental risks.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Stabilise against stronger neighbours, align the economy with magical prerequisites, then advance research and apotheosis.
player_overview.overview: Varamhar begins with a powerful mage ruler but must first face stronger neighbours. Build an academy, organise the mages and direct commercial resources so that magic becomes a national project rather than a personal talent, then attempt the ultimate goal of manufacturing a god. The experiments can damage the land, while the ruler and preparation conditions determine the outcome; the whole country must support this dangerous research.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy mage rulers, research projects and apotheosis narratives.
signature_features: The academy, mage organisations and material resources jointly support the divine project.
A powerful mage ruler determines both the opening opportunities and the later risks.
Apotheosis has different outcomes, and the experiment is not a cost-free reward.
player_overview.tagline: Turn a small Sun Elf kingdom into a national laboratory and try to manufacture a god with your own hands.

reasons: The academy, mage organisations and material resources jointly support the divine project.

warnings: It is a poor fit for players who dislike multiple prerequisites or ruler and experimental risks.

positive_indicators: Investment in academies and magical education
values.rationale: The academy, cities and research provide public benefits; the divine project causes severe devastation in province 609 and reduces development, while the research politics permit high-risk costs. The evidence does not establish that the entire population is treated as a resource, and no deduction is made merely for being Sun Elves, religious or expansionist.
red_flags: Experiments cause severe devastation and development loss in a province
Apotheosis outcomes are tiered by preparation, and some paths end the original ruler's life
